title: Wide cross-platform discovery pass 50
summary: Personally review 17 roots: add 11 projects, consolidate three lineage duplicates and defer three candidates.
notes: Root personally searched 20 platform/type queries and inspected 17 selected new or alternate roots: 11 additions, three lineage duplicates and three deferrals. Screening also rejected already tracked roots and irrelevant keyword matches. Amiga, CPC, Spectrum, BBC/Electron, C64, DOS, PC-98, Saturn and Apple II/IIgs sources were considered; this is not a claim of exhaustive platform coverage. No discovery worker used. Read-only upstream source inspection, no builds or proprietary image downloads. Each cached proof is bound to a separately fetched commit, matching pinned file listing and Git blob hash. Ingestion lessons: GitHub fork flags alone do not distinguish a meaningful continuation from a duplicate; follow explicit upstream/successor links. Bare README goals and stale copied documentation are insufficient. Distinguish original source preservation, native developer utilities, decompiler output and playable reconstruction. Hardware-independent input formats do not imply host CPU minima. Restricted assembler support, colour truncation, missing historical programs and custom checksum semantics are retained as limitations. No baked-emulation classification is inferred from I/O shims, tape animation or debugger integration. Source review does not prove binary matching or robustness. Six previously decided URLs are represented by updated source reviews rather than duplicate decision rows. The earlier DOSBox integration deferral is addressed by inspecting the manifest and actual debugger protocol implementation; its promotion supersedes that dated uncertainty. Existing duplicate/exclusion decisions remain preserved.

sources.reason: Amiga SWOS 96/97 analysis combines annotated assembly, generated C and IDA/Ghidra export and repair scripts. Generated decompiler C is not a finished native C port.

Continuation of XenonTranslation/tools includes script extraction/compression and Shift-JIS translation insertion. Author reports story translated and inserted, with main load menu and omake still excluded.

Single-file browser tool implements SCR conversion, BASIC tokenization, TAP/TZX generation, WAV synthesis/decoding and a limited Z80 assembler. Unsupported instruction forms explicitly fail; not a full assembler or hardware-fidelity claim.
Preserved early-1990s native +3/+D/DISCiPLE disk and tape conversion assembly, adapted to z88dk z80asm directives. Actual directory/selection and DOS-call implementation is present.
Native C64 utility transfers D71/D81 images from a 1541 Ultimate 2 to physical drives. Source uses KERNAL channels and block-write commands; C128 burst-mode version is only planned.
Converts compatible C64 disk programs to EasyFlash cartridges using KERNAL load hooks and cartridge banking. Only LOAD-based programs are supported, not arbitrary custom loaders.
Raylib viewer maps C64 disk sectors and BAM usage, with checksum diagnostics for the author’s custom backup logs. Directory analysis and health indicators remain unfinished.

65816 tracing disassembler handles raw/OMF segments, tracks M/X operand widths, names IIgs tool calls with fingerprints and iterates from user-supplied entrypoints. Companion 2mg extracts ProDOS images.
Swift image converter emits Merlin-compatible 4bpp graphics, palette setup and draw code for IIgs memory. RGB channels are reduced to four bits.

Native grep-like utility integrates regex and argument parsing with GS/OS file types, wildcards and recursive search. Implements a bounded regex/option subset rather than complete GNU grep compatibility.

Collection of lightly modified 2CDT/iDSK sources; unique capabilities beyond the tracked tool lineage and mastering workflow not established. Retain for lineage review, not another independent implementation.
